title: Holiday blackout & mini-roll cadence — checklist + rehearsal notes
body:
Purpose:
This note captures a lightweight ops playbook for holiday blackout windows and a paired small-batch (mini-roll) cadence we want to validate in the next 6 weeks. Aim: minimize blast radius during customer-facing quiet windows while preserving the ability to ship critical fixes.

Context / motivation:
- Past incident (Dec 2025) showed we can be overly conservative (2-week freeze) which delays urgent fixes and piles up technical debt.
- We need a repeatable mini-roll cadence that allows a tight change path for emergency fixes with strict gate checks and simulated rehearsals before/within blackout windows.
- This doc is intentionally pragmatic: checklist + short rehearsal calendar + release-note draft template for any mini-roll during a blackout.

High-level policy proposal (short):
1) Full blackout window = no non-critical changes. Exceptions: security patches, customer-impacting hotfixes, and infra safety fixes approved by on-call lead + SRE.
2) Mini-roll lane: a narrow path for emergency fixes that meets the checklist below and uses canary traffic of <= 1% for 30 minutes with telemetry gating.
3) Approval model: on-call lead (primary) + SRE duty + product manager (if user-visible). If any approver is unreachable, fallback is on-call engineering director (phone or Slack call).

Mini-roll requirements (must all pass):
- PR checklist:
  - Change scope <= 3 files or single service patch
  - Unit and integration tests green
  - Release script run locally + smoke script success
- Observability:
  - New metrics instrumented or existing metrics confirmed (latency, error-rate, token-emit-rate)
  - Dashboard snapshot URL included in PR description
- Safety gates:
  - Canary route configured, <= 1% traffic
  - Circuit breaker threshold defined in PR (error-rate %, latency p99 ms)
  - Rollback procedure written in PR description (one-liner + ticket link)
- Release ops:
  - Release owner assigned (not the original author)
  - 30-min post-deploy watch at minimum
  - Pager duty rotation ensured (name + contact in PR)
- Communication:
  - Slack #release-alerts ping + thread starter with link to release notes draft
  - Email to CS on-call if change might touch customer journeys

Telemetry gating thresholds (example templates):
- Errors: no more than +0.5% absolute error-rate vs baseline for 30m rolling window
- Latency: p99 increase <= +50ms absolute vs baseline for 30m window
- Token throughput: no degradation >5% in top-5 tail routes
- If any gate trips during canary -> immediate rollback and incident stub (link to template)

Rollback decision flow (quick):
1) Canary telemetry trip OR user-reported regression -> owner attempts quick mitigation rollback (revert deploy).
2) If rollback fails or root cause unclear: declare P1 and notify incident commander.
3) Post-incident: run a short retro within 48 hours and capture follow-ups in REL-842.

Pre-holiday rehearsal calendar (60–30–7–1 schedule):
- T-minus 60 days: policy sync with SRE + product (reviewed, any major changes flagged)
  Owner: Samira. Deliverable: one-pager to #eng-release (link). Target: 2026-09-01
- T-minus 30 days: run a dry-run mini-roll (non-prod -> staging -> canary) with emergency patch simulated.
  Participants: release engineer, SRE duty, on-call lead, CS on-call. Target: 2026-10-01
- T-minus 7 days: confirm holiday on-call roster + silent-alert simulation (small traffic spike during canary)
  Deliverable: roster doc + simulation report. Target: 2026-10-24
- T-minus 1 day: final checklist + quick smoke on canary route
  Deliverable: Go/No-Go note in thread and final release notes draft. Target: 2026-10-30

Staffing + contact map (example):
- Primary release owner: Samira Patel (pager +1)
- SRE duty (rotation): Ethan Morales (backup: Luca Romano)
- Product approver: Priya Iyer
- CS on-call: Maya Thompson

Release notes draft template (to be pasted into PR thread):
- Title: [mini-roll] <service> patch — short description (one line)
- Why: brief root cause or need (1-2 lines)
- Impact: customer-visible? internal-only? expected degradation?
- Rollout: canary -> 1% -> gradual (owner will push)
- Telemetry gates: listed thresholds + dashboard links
- Rollback plan: steps + ticket id
- Contacts: owner, SRE, PM, CS on-call

Quick rehearsal script (engineer-facing):
1) Create a tiny staging change (config flag flip or circuit-breaker tweak) and a PR labeled "mini-roll/dry-run"
2) Attach test dashboard snapshot and local smoke run output
3) Request canary via deploy UI (1% traffic) and observe for 30 minutes
4) If stable, promote to 10% for 20m and then to 100% when clear; if unstable, perform rollback and note timings
5) Fill the rehearsal notes template (time, who, symptoms, action taken) in the PR

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- Decide exact canary window durations (30m vs 15m). Ops team leaning to 30m but product wants 15m for speed.
- Need small automation: a one-click checklist in the deploy UI that enforces the gates (maybe GH-725)
- Confirm CS on-call escalation policy for global customers in APAC timezone during our blackout period (who wakes up?).

References and artifacts to copy into final policy doc:
- REL-842 (ticket for holiday deck and policy)
- GH-725 (deploy UI checklist workstream)
- Confluence draft: /release/holiday-policy (current living doc)

Field notes from last rehearsal (6/15/2026) — quick summary:
- We simulated a config-based throttle change for routing. Canary at 1% tripped alerting from synthetic probes after ~12m (false positive due to probe flakiness).
- Action: rollback completed in 6m. Post-mortem: tune synthetic probe thresholds and add metadata so alerts ignore known rehearsal probes.
- Follow-ups: add rehearsal-probe flag to synthetic suite, update doc. (Assigned: Luca)

If you plan to use this for the upcoming winter window, please add comments below and flag any stakeholder I missed. I'll convert to a formal runbook after two successful rehearsals.

-- Samira

Notes to reviewers: informal draft. Feel free to inline corrections; we want a lightweight mechanism rather than another heavy policy doc.
